newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's PTTEP plans $200 mln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's PTTEP plans $200 mln in bonds.

text.p: PTT Exploration and Production Plc, the exploration arm of the Petroleum Authority of Thailand, plans to issue bonds in foreign markets worth $200 million this year, its president Prajya Phinyavat said on Wednesday.

He said the issue of the bonds would be made whether or not Moody's Investor Service downgraded its credit rating. Moody's said on February 14 that it had placed PTTEP's A2 senior unsecured rating under review for a possible downgrade.
"We are mulling issuing Samurai bonds, but it depends, it could also be Yankee or European debentured," Prajya said.
The proceeds from the bonds issue would be used to finance PTTEP's various petroleum exploration and production activities, he added. The company plans to invest 35 billion baht between 1997 to 2001.
In September 1996, PTTEP International, which is another unit of the Petroleum Autority of Thailand, issued unsubordinated bonds in the United States which were guaranteed by PTTEP.
The notes were priced at 10-year U.S. Treaury plus 85 basis points and offered a coupon of 7.625 percent per annum.
